An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"

{ "name": "meeting-room-booking", "version": "1.0.0", "private": true, "type": "module", "scripts": { "start": "node server.mjs", "test": "node --test \"test/**/*.test.mjs\"" } } Room bookings

Room bookings

    # Decisions — owner: supervisor - File layout: `server.mjs` (backend), `public/index.html` + `public/app.js` (frontend; server reads them and serves at `GET /` and `GET /app.js`, resolved relative to server.mjs via import.meta.url), `test/*.test.mjs` (testing), `package.json` (`"type": "module"`, `"start": "node server.mjs"`, `"test": "node --test test/"`), `README.md` (docs). - Data file layout: `{"nextId": , "bookings": [ {id, room, title, date, start, end}, ... ]}`. On load, validate strictly (object, integer nextId >= 1, bookings array of well-formed bookings with id < nextId); anything else → `cannot read data file `. - Save: write a temp file next to the data file then rename (atomic); a failed save rolls back memory. All mutations serialized through one in-process queue/lock. - Strict readings: where a spec line reads two ways, build the stricter reading. - 2026-11-02 · frontend · A success-status reply (200) whose JSON lacks the expected `rooms`/`bookings` array shows `Request failed.` in `#error` and changes nothing else (latest list fetch only). Why: spec is silent; avoids an uncaught TypeError and matches the "error message otherwise" fallback. - 2026-11-02 · frontend · `node --test test/` (directory arg) fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on this Node 22.23; the package.json "test" script should be `node --test` (default discovery) or a glob. Why: verified by running it. - 2026-11-02 · backend · package.json "test" is `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"` (glob, not default discovery). Why: `node --test test/` fails on Node 22; default discovery would also run `test/helpers/*.mjs` and any `.team/near-miss/` copies matching `*.test.mjs`. Test files must be named `*.test.mjs`. - 2026-11-02 · backend · Strict readings: ENOTDIR on DATA_FILE is not ENOENT (gives `cannot read data file`); HEAD on known paths is 405; a data file with overlapping, duplicate-id, untrimmed-title or extra-key bookings is an invalid layout. Why: build the stricter reading. - 2026-11-02 · testing · Tests assert the stricter readings: a data file with an extra top-level key, or a UTF-8 BOM before valid JSON, is not this server's layout (exit 1, `cannot read data file `); `​` is a valid 1-unit title (String.prototype.trim keeps it); a Content-Type padded with U+00A0 is 415 (only spaces/tabs are stripped). Why: the server writes exactly `{nextId, bookings}` with no BOM, and the spec names trim() for titles but spaces/tabs for the media type. - 2026-11-02 · testing · Child-process tests wait for `'close'`, not `'exit'`, before reading stdout/stderr; raw-TCP requests do not half-close the socket. Why: `'exit'` can fire before stdio drains (flaky empty stderr), and node:http aborts a request whose client sent FIN before the reply. # Backend API notes — owner: backend — 2026-11-02 Spec: `.team/notes/spec.md` is the source of truth; this note only records implementation choices. ## Running - `node server.mjs` (or `npm start`) starts the server. `server.mjs` exports nothing; importing it starts the server. - Tests: `npm test` runs `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`. Plain `node --test test/` does NOT work on Node 22 (a directory argument is treated as a file). Test files must be named `*.test.mjs` under `test/`; helpers in `test/helpers/` are not run as tests. ## Env vars - `PORT`: unset/empty means 3000. Only ASCII digits, value <= 65535, else one stderr line `invalid PORT: `, exit 1. `PORT=0` means the OS picks the port; the stdout line shows the real port. - `DATA_FILE`: unset/empty means `bookings.json`, resolved against the cwd. ENOENT means start empty (the file is not created). Any other read error, or content not in the layout below, gives stderr `cannot read data file `, exit 1. - Bind failure gives stderr `cannot listen on 127.0.0.1:: `, exit 1. - stdout: only `listening on http://127.0.0.1:\n`. Unexpected request errors are logged to stderr as one line. ## Data file layout `{"nextId": = 1>, "bookings": [{"id","room","title","date","start","end"}, ...]}` Loading is strict: the top level must have exactly the keys nextId and bookings; each booking needs exactly those 6 keys, a safe-integer id in 1..nextId-1, unique ids, valid room/date/times, end > start, an already-trimmed title of 1-80 chars, and no two stored bookings may overlap. Anything else counts as "not in this server's layout". ## Saving - Written only on a successful POST create or DELETE remove. Writes `...tmp` in the same folder (flag `wx`), then renames it over the data file; on failure the temp file is removed and the reply is 500 `internal error`. - Memory (bookings and nextId) changes only after the save succeeds. All mutations run one at a time through an in-process promise queue (overlap check + save inside the queue). ## Static files - `GET /` serves `public/index.html` (`text/html; charset=utf-8`), `GET /app.js` serves `public/app.js` (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`). Paths are resolved relative to `server.mjs` via `import.meta.url`, read per request. A missing file gives 500 `internal error`; the server keeps running. Other methods on these paths get 405. ## Strict readings taken - ENOTDIR (a path component is a file) is not ENOENT, so it gives `cannot read data file`. - HEAD on any known path gets 405 (no auto-HEAD for GET routes). - Overlapping stored bookings in the data file count as an invalid layout. # Frontend page — owner: frontend — 2026-11-02 Files: `public/index.html` (served at `GET /`), `public/app.js` (served at `GET /app.js`). Tests: `test/page-static.test.mjs` (HTML/script constraints), `test/page.test.mjs` (app.js in node:vm), helper `test/helpers/fake-dom.mjs` (fake DOM elements, fake fetch with manual resolve, `loadPage`, `flush`). ## Element ids - `booking-form` (form, novalidate) containing `room` (select, empty), `title` (text), `date` (date), `start` (time), `end` (time), `book` (submit button "Book"); labels Room/Title/Date/Start/End. - Outside the form: `filter-date` (date, label "Show date"), `show-all` (button "Show all"), `booking-list` (ul), `error` (p, role=alert, empty). - `` is the last element in body.
